audit_title: VISION 100M Token Consumption and Discrepancy Investigation

loss_and_entropy_analysis.interpretation: Initial loss (9.14) reflects near-uniform random distribution over 8,192 tokens. Final loss (7.81) reflects early emergence of unigram frequency bias, reducing entropy from ~9.01 to 7.81 but remaining far above fluent generation threshold (~2.0-3.5).

collapse_mechanism_investigation.explanation: A 98M parameter model initialized randomly requires at least 100M-2B tokens to form syntax and semantic attention circuits. In 20,480 tokens across 10 optimizer updates, gradient descent minimized cross-entropy by biasing the output layer towards high-frequency unigram tokens (such as digit '1' and whitespace), causing argmax greedy decoding to collapse into repeating '11111111111111111111111111111111'.
collapse_mechanism_investigation.benchmark_score_0_of_240_explained: Because greedy decoding generated '11111111...', all 240 independent evaluation probes (which test arithmetic answers like '467', Python functions like 'def add(a, b):', Java methods, logic proofs, etc.) scored 0.00%. This is an expected mathematical consequence of severe under-training.

remediation_requirements.phase_1_immediate: Audit complete training pipeline (RoPE, causal mask, label shifting, loss masking) using a tiny overfit diagnostic test to prove mathematical correctness of learning circuits.
remediation_requirements.phase_2_recovery: Warm-start or curriculum train the 100M architecture on focused high-density instruction/math/code tokens and verify loss reduction and token diversity.
remediation_requirements.phase_3_scaling: Map compute requirements for 10M-token local pretraining vs cloud GPU cluster compute.
